name: Diazepam
executiveSummary: Benzodiazepine. Adult status: **5–10 mg IV** slow; repeat every 10–15 min (usual cumulative max **30 mg**). Pediatric status: **0.1–0.3 mg/kg** IV (max **5–10 mg**/dose). Rectal/PO by indication. Respiratory depression risk.
indications:
## Indications

- Status epilepticus / acute seizures.
- Anxiety, procedural sedation, muscle spasm, alcohol withdrawal (regimens).

## Precautions

- Respiratory/CNS depression — have airway support. Paradoxical effect in children.
- IV: **not >5 mg/min** adults; precipitates in some diluents; phlebitis.
- Pregnancy/lactation: risk; prefer alternatives when possible.

> Antidote: flumazenil (selective use; may precipitate seizures).

adulto.presentation: Ampoule 5 mg/mL; tabs 2–5–10 mg; rectal gel/solution.
adulto.dose: Status: **5–10 mg IV**; repeat every **10–15 min** until control (usual cumulative max **30 mg**). Anxiety/sedation PO: **2–10 mg** every 6–8 h. Continuous ICU infusion: **0.1–0.2 mg/kg/h** (less common vs midazolam).
adulto.administration: Very slow IV (large vein). Rectal if no access. PO with food.
adulto.notes: IM absorption erratic — prefer IV/rectal for seizures.

pediatrico.presentation: Ampoule 5 mg/mL; tabs; compounded 2 mg/mL; rectal.
pediatrico.dose: Status IV: **0.1–0.3 mg/kg** every 5–10 min (max <5 years **5 mg**/dose; ≥5 years **10 mg**). Immediate rectal: 2–5 years **0.5 mg/kg**; 6–11 years **0.3 mg/kg**; ≥12 years **0.2 mg/kg**. Procedural PO sedation: **0.2–0.3 mg/kg** (max **10 mg**) 45–60 min before. Anxiety PO: **0.12–0.8 mg/kg/day** every 6–8 h.
pediatrico.administration: IV ≤1–2 mg/min in children; continuous dilution ~0.2 mg/mL in NS.

neonatal.dose: Seizures: **0.1–0.3 mg/kg** slow IV — prefer phenobarbital/others per NNU protocol.

stability:
## Stability

- Opened ampoule: discard leftover. Dilutions: follow label (plastic adsorption).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Somnolence, ataxia, respiratory depression, hypotension, thrombophlebitis, paradoxical irritability, dependence.
